decisions.reason: The resin injection unit sits squarely in the firm's core plural-component business, and keeping a product that already has its own page costs little, so the option is still worth holding.

The second resin injection unit adds a variant to an established line at low carrying cost, and no evidence shows it has failed, though overlap with Product A slightly raises the chance it is consolidated.
Automatic airless guns are a staple accessory that supports equipment and spare-parts sales, so retaining it costs little and protects the core business.
A manual airless gun is a core consumable-type product with steady demand and minimal carrying cost, so dropping it brings no benefit.
The air-assisted airless line with several models fits the firm's central application technology and remained on its own page, which suggests continued commitment.

The data logger was reduced from its own page to a mere mention, which hints at weaker results, but digital monitoring may still gain value, so the cheap option is held for now despite an elevated drop risk.
